context:
Goal: price changes you can trust to send in one press.
Problem (money): a raise past your 25% limit is cut to the limit; a fall past it keeps its full depth. How deep a fall goes sets what a card sells for.
Based on (read): the spec's 'a cap both ways': a move past the limit waits in Needs you, unticked.
Today in the mockup: a fall past the limit keeps its full depth and waits for your tick, such as 'Market down 30% since listed, past your 25% limit.'

options.gain: You see the real market drop, and nothing goes without your tick.
options.how: A fall past the limit shows its full drop in Needs you, unticked.
options.label: Full depth, waits for your tick
options.lose: One tick sends a drop bigger than 25%.

options.gain: No single send drops a price more than 25%.
options.how: A fall past the limit is cut to 25% and waits in Needs you.
options.label: Stop at the limit, like raises
options.lose: A card that truly fell stays over market until the next pass.

ref: pricing-suggest spec section 1 (a cap both ways); list mockup notes, point 7
title: Does a price fall past the 25% limit also stop at the limit?
why: The tick already guards it, and a card stuck over market does not sell.
